item.title: Introduction to MySQL
item.description: MySQL is a widely used relational database management system (RDBMS) that is used to store and manage data for a variety of applications. It is an open-source software that is developed and maintained by Oracle Corporation. MySQL is one of the most popular RDBMS solutions in the world, and it is used by millions of developers and organizations. In this blog post, we will explore what MySQL is, how it works, and why it is such an important tool for developers and businesses.

item.title: MySQL SELECT FROM
item.description: Introduction to MySQL SELECT FROM statement The SELECT statement allows you to select data from one or more tables. To write a SELECT statement in MySQL, you use this syntax: SELECT select_list FROM table_name; In this syntax: First, specify one or more columns from which you want to select data after the SELECT keyword. If the select_list has multiple columns, you need to separate them by a comma ,. Second, specify the name of the table from which you want to select data after the FROM keyword.

item.title: MySQL ORDER BY - VS Code
item.description: Introduction to the MySQL ORDER BY clause When you use the SELECT statement to query data from a table, the order of rows in the result set is unspecified. To sort the rows in the result set, you add the ORDER BY clause to the SELECT statement. The following illustrates the syntax of the ORDER BY clause: SELECT select_list FROM table_name ORDER BY column1 [ASC|DESC], column2 [ASC|DESC], ...; In this syntax, you specify one or more columns that you want to sort after the ORDER BY clause.

item.title: MySQL NOT IN Operator - VS Code
item.description: In this guide, we’ll explore the MySQL NOT IN operator, a valuable tool for checking if a specific value is absent from a given list. Understanding the MySQL NOT IN Operator The NOT IN operator works by negating the IN operator. It checks if a value does not match any values in a provided list. If there’s no match, it returns 1; otherwise, it returns 0. Let’s delve into a simple example to understand its application.

item.title: MySQL AS Aliases - VS Code
item.description: MySQL, a commonly used relational database management system, offers a usefull feature known as aliases. Aliases allow you to assign temporary names to columns or tables in your queries, enhancing readability and simplifying complex expressions. Understanding Column AS Aliases Column Alias Syntax In MySQL, column aliases are utilized to assign a temporary name to a column in the result set. The basic syntax is as follows: SELECT [column_1 | expression] AS descriptive_name FROM table_name; You can also assign an alias to an expression, and if the alias contains spaces, it should be enclosed in quotes.

item.title: MySQL BETWEEN Operator - VS Code
item.description: MySQL: BETWEEN Operator In this tutorial, we’ll explore the practical applications of the MySQL BETWEEN operator to determine whether a value falls within a specified range. Introduction to MySQL BETWEEN Operator The BETWEEN operator is a logical tool that checks if a value is within a designated range. Its syntax is straightforward: value BETWEEN low AND high; The BETWEEN operator evaluates to 1 if: value >= low AND value <= high; Otherwise, it returns 0.

item.title: MySQL IS NULL Operator - VS Code
item.description: Introduction to MySQL IS NULL Operator: In the world of databases, understanding the MySQL IS NULL operator is crucial. This operator helps determine if a value is NULL or not, playing a significant role in SQL queries. Basic Syntax of IS NULL Operator: The syntax is straightforward. When you want to check if a value is NULL, you use the expression value IS NULL. If the value is indeed NULL, the expression returns true; otherwise, it returns false.

item.title: MySQL LIMIT Clause - VS Code
item.description: Introduction to MySQL LIMIT Clause The MySQL LIMIT clause is a valuable tool in SQL queries to control the number of rows retrieved. It plays a crucial role in scenarios such as pagination, obtaining top or bottom results, and fetching rows based on specific conditions. Basic Syntax of LIMIT Clause The basic syntax involves specifying the starting point (offset) and the maximum number of rows to return. The default starting point is 0.

item.title: MySQL LIKE Operator - VS Code
item.description: The MySQL LIKE operator is a usefull tool for querying data based on specified patterns. Let’s explore its usage with common examples. MySQL LIKE Operator Basics** The LIKE operator checks if a string contains a specific pattern. The two main wildcard characters are % and _. % matches any string of zero or more characters. _ matches any single character. Examples of Using MySQL LIKE Operator** Example 1: Finding Names Starting with ‘A’ SELECT employeeNumber, lastName, firstName FROM employees WHERE firstName LIKE 'A%'; This query retrieves employees whose first names start with ‘A’.

item.title: Create PIVOT Table in MySQL Step-by-Step Guide
item.description: PIVOT table in MySQL use for data analysis and summarization. They allow users to quickly summarize data by different dimensions and provide a more detailed view of the data. PIVOT tables are especially useful for analyzing large datasets, as they can help to quickly identify trends and patterns. How Useful the PIVOT Table in MySQL MySQL’s PIVOT table feature has a variety of uses. For example, it allows users to quickly and easily summarize large amounts of data in a concise and organized way.
